articles.title: Microsoft November 2026 Patch Tuesday Addresses Critical RCE Flaws and Outlook Zero-Day Attacks
articles.summary:
Microsoft released its November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates, addressing 1,093 newly disclosed vulnerabilities across Windows, Office, SQL Server, SharePoint, Exchange Server, Azure services, and developer tools. The release includes 63 Critical flaws, 1,029 Important issues, and one Moderate vulnerability, including an actively exploited Outlook zero-day that exposes authentication information. articles.title: Microsoft Outlook Zero-Day Vulnerability Actively Exploited to Steal NTLM Authentication Hashes
articles.summary:
Microsoft has patched an actively exploited Outlook zero-day that lets attackers steal Windows authentication information through a malicious message file. Tracked as CVE-2026-124194, the spoofing vulnerability was released on November 10, 2026. articles.summary:

articles.title: Critical Fortinet Vulnerabilities Allow Unauthenticated Attackers to Execute Remote Code on FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer
articles.summary:
Fortinet disclosed critical vulnerabilities in FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, and FortiOS on November 10, 2026, including flaws that could let attackers execute code without logging in. The disclosures cover management APIs, device communication, routing, and specific high availability configurations. Exposure depends on enabled services, network access, and deployment settings. articles.title: New GhostFrame Malware Targets VMware ESXi Servers to Steal Credentials and Hijack Virtual Machines
articles.summary:
Researchers have uncovered GhostFrame, a previously undocumented command-and-control (C2) and post-exploitation framework that turns compromised VMware ESXi hosts into platforms for credential theft, virtual machine control, and network intrusion. Insikt Group’s November 10 report links its use to TAG-218, whose activity overlaps with Settra ransomware. The framework requires existing root access; it does not exploit […]

articles.title: China-Linked CopperDragon Malware Framework Targets Critical Infrastructure Across Europe, Asia, and Latin America
articles.summary:
Research has tied three seemingly unrelated espionage campaigns to a single supplier of Chinese-nexus tooling, which it tracks as CopperDragon. It may act as a “digital quartermaster,” supplying tools to several China-nexus actors, including FamousSparrow, Earth Estries, TropicTrooper and UAT-9244.
